newsitem.title: GERMANY: Austria sees Schengen membership, despite criticism.
newsitem.headline: Austria sees Schengen membership, despite criticism.

text.p: Austria said on Thursday it expected neighbouring countries to drop their objections to it signing up to the Schengen accord, which allows passport-free travel among a group of western European countries.
Interior Minister Karl Schloegl told German radio stations Austria had done enough to shore up its borders with its eastern neighbours to become a full Schengen member this year.
Speaking ahead of a summit with leaders from Germany and Italy, Schloegl told Bavarian radio: "We want clarity. We are ready for Schengen and have invested heavily to achieve that."

Austria has come under fire from the southern German state of Bavaria, which has said it has not done enough to bar illegal immigrants crossing into western Europe from the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary and Slovenia.
But Schloegl said Austria's border controls met the same standards as those of other European states.
"Austria's security measures in relation to the former east bloc states are in no way too lax. We have made efforts in recent months to reach the best possible standard," he said.

"We want to do everything possible to achieve security for all European states, but above all for our own security: we do not want illegal travel into and out of Austria, and we do not want organised crime to penetrate our borders."
He said he was optimistic that an agreement could be reached at the summit, which was to be held later on Thursday in the Austrian Alpine town of Innsbruck.
"I expect that we will reach an agreement today which guarantees that Austria will become a full member of Schengen this year," Schloegl said.
